actions_taken.action: FOUND AND FIXED a FUSE-staleness data-loss risk in monitor/social/search-rankings.json. The FUSE-mounted workspace copy of this file was stale by 34 days (last write reflected in the FUSE `runs` array stopped at 2026-06-19), while the file's actual current data lives in a separate top-level `rankings` array that only exists in git HEAD (verified via a fresh --depth 1 clone: 14 entries through 2026-07-23). Had I naively appended today's entry to the stale FUSE copy per the prompt's 'append, so we see trends' instruction without cross-checking git HEAD first, I would have silently dropped 15 days of tracked search-ranking history (2026-07-05 through 2026-07-23) when workspace-sync next pushed this whole-file smart_copy to git. Fetched the true git HEAD content, appended today's entry to the correct `rankings` array in the same schema as the 2026-07-23 entry, and wrote the merged, complete file back to the FUSE workspace path.
actions_taken.reasoning: This file has accumulated three top-level containers over its history (`runs` -- legacy, dead since ~2026-06-19; `entries` -- legacy, 11 entries, unclear currency; `rankings` -- the live one, appended to daily since at least 2026-06-17). None of this is documented in CLAUDE.md's file-ownership tables, and nothing flags which array is canonical. This is exactly the kind of silent schema drift that has bitten this pipeline before (queue-history mass-delete, status.json chimera writes). Filing as a human/tinker-attention item below rather than unilaterally deleting the dead `runs`/`entries` arrays -- they may have historical value and this file's ownership isn't clearly single-writer.
